summary: Yuko Kamishima specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Tokyo (~1991–2000) and as a research student under Ekai Kawaguchi, and held a post at Ritsumeikan University.

Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College. She held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001) and taught Catherine Ludvik.

Yuko Yokochi works in Indology, having studied at the University of Tokyo (MA) and the University of Groningen (PhD, 2004) under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. She served as Associate Professor at Kyoto University (attested 2002–2022).
Yulian Zeng works in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2010), where she studied under MA supervisor Kirill Solonin.
Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She was a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).

Yumi Nakamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She was a researcher (公募研究員) at Ryukoku University in 2012 and also studied there as a research student (研究生, attested 2014).
Yumiko Ishihama specializes in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University (~1981–1989) and later held a post there around 1996.

Yun Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University in 2006. She served as Librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).
Yungfen Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned a PhD at Columbia University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü (attested 2011).

Yuri Levada studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (~1947–1952). His career included positions at Moscow State University (~1956–1972), the Institute of Sociology (~1968–1972), VTSIOM (~1988–2003), the Levada Center (~2003–2006), and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.
Yusen Kashiwahara worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Otani University (~1938–1943) and later served there as a professor (~1954–1987).

Yusho Miyasaka, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe. He held posts at Koyasan University (1954; 1965–1967), Nagoya University (1977–1984), Chisan Denpōin (1987), and Shuchiin University (2001).

Yusho Wakahara specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami and held posts at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and Ryukoku University (assistant professor attested 1987–1999; professor attested 2011–2013).
Yutai Ikeda worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He held an academic post at Otani University and was an Emeritus Professor at Doho University (attested 2006).

Yutaka Hirata specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, earning a doctorate from Kyushu University. He worked at the Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1959–1969), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1994–2004).

Yutaka Iwamoto specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying at Kyoto University (~1930–1933). He held professorships at Tokyo University of Science (~1963–1967), Tokai University (~1967–1974), Kyoto Tachibana University (~1974–1980), and Soka University (~1980–1986).

Yutaka Kanazawa specializes in Buddhist studies and completed a PhD at Ryukoku University in 2010. His teachers included Kogi Kudara, Hōgei Mitsukawa, Isao Shimizu, and doctoral supervisors Shoryu Katsura and Masaaki Noni.
Yutaka Kawasaki works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Seio Okuda and held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024).

Indologist and linguist Yutaka Ochihara studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Louis Renou, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard. He was a professor at Kyoto University (1972–1986) and Professeur étranger at Collège de France (1985).

Yutaka Takagi specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University (~1970–1999).
